# Gas City (`gc`), the orchestration SDK that replaced Gas Town (`gt`).
#
# Gas Town's last release (v1.2.1, Jun 2026) predates beads 1.3, and a fresh
# `gt install` on bd 1.3.x deadlocks on bd's dirty-table migration guard
# (gastownhall/beads#6089). Gas City is where the work moved: its v1.5.0
# deps.env pins bd v1.3.1 and wants dolt >= 2.1.0.
#
# Built from source to carry ../patches/gascity-runtime-dir.patch, which adds
# GC_RUNTIME_DIR. Upstream couples the runtime dir to GC_HOME: any GC_HOME off
# ~/.gc counts as an "isolated" home and moves the supervisor socket and lock
# under it instead of $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gc. env.nix relocates GC_HOME to XDG
# state, so without the patch sockets would live in ~/.local/state.
#
# The name: oh-my-zsh's git plugin aliases `gc` to `git commit -v`, so in
# interactive zsh `gc` stays git commit and Gas City is typed as `gascity`.
# The binary must still be on PATH as `gc`: Gas City calls itself by that name
# in the hooks and prompts it hands agents (`gc prime`, `gc hook`, `gc mail`,
# ~89 files at v1.5.0) and in a few exec("gc") calls. Hooks run under sh, where
# the alias does not apply, so they reach the real binary.
{ pkgs }:

pkgs.buildGoModule rec {
  pname = "gascity";
  version = "1.5.0";
  commit = "f66474617d2bb7fbe51a3d746da5f3ceab2b8517";

  src = pkgs.fetchFromGitHub {
    owner = "gastownhall";
    repo = "gascity";
    rev = "v${version}";
    hash = "sha256-le/REDACTED";
  };

  patches = [
    ../patches/gascity-runtime-dir.patch
    # Usage metrics compiled off (RolloutDefaultOff: collection fails closed
    # whatever the env or `gc metrics on` say). Local policy, not for upstream;
    # it flips upstream's TestOpenProductionAndPreparationAreLazyAndNonCreating,
    # which expects the default-on first-run notice. env.nix's
    # GC_DISABLE_USAGE_METRICS=1 is the second layer.
    ../patches/gascity-no-usage-metrics.patch
  ];

  vendorHash = "REDACTED/m2QvJcwYzmNFUs=";

  subPackages = [ "cmd/gc" ];

  env.CGO_ENABLED = "0";
  env.GOTOOLCHAIN = "local";

  # Mirrors .goreleaser.yml. compiledReleaseTag classifies telemetry as a
  # release (vs canary) build; left empty it would report as a dev build.
  ldflags = [
    "-s" "-w"
    "-X main.version=v${version}"
    "-X main.commit=${commit}"
    "-X main.date=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    "-X github.com/gastownhall/gascity/internal/productmetrics.compiledReleaseTag=${version}"
  ];

  # Upstream's cmd/gc suite drives tmux, dolt and a live supervisor; it does not
  # run in the sandbox. The patch's own tests were run against the source tree.
  doCheck = false;

  postInstall = ''
    ln -s gc $out/bin/gascity
  '';

  meta = {
    description = "Orchestration-builder SDK for multi-agent coding workflows";
    homepage = "https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity";
    license = pkgs.lib.licenses.mit;
    mainProgram = "gc";
  };
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the Gas City toolchain (gc + bd + dolt) landing on the Gas City
# hosts (fujiwara, utsuho) and nowhere else.
#
# Gas City is a tmux fleet of Claude sessions that bills while it runs, so it
# lives only on the boxes meant to host it. Two ways this breaks quietly:
#
#   * a Gas City host loses a piece. gc shells out to `bd` for every bead and runs a
#     managed `dolt` for the city, so gc without either evaluates fine and then
#     dies at `gc init`. Cases 1-2 check all three are in each closure.
#
#   * the gate widens. Dropping the hostname guard puts gc on every host, and
#     nothing errors. Case 3 checks a laptop (shiori) carries none of them.
#
# Evaluation only (--max-jobs 0): this never builds a derivation.
#
#   ./tests/gascity-packages.sh
set -u

repo="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

fails=0; n=0
ok()  { n=$((n+1)); printf 'ok %d - %s\n' "$n" "$1"; }
bad() { n=$((n+1)); fails=$((fails+1)); printf 'FAIL %d - %s\n' "$n" "$1"; }

names() { # names <host> -- space-separated pnames of home.packages
  nix eval --max-jobs 0 --raw "$repo#homeConfigurations.$1.config.home.packages" \
    --apply 'ps: builtins.concatStringsSep " " (map (p: p.pname or p.name or "") ps)'
}

for host in fujiwara utsuho; do
  have=$(names "$host") || { echo "could not evaluate $host" >&2; exit 1; }
  missing=""
  for p in gascity beads dolt; do
    case " $have " in *" $p "*) ;; *) missing="$missing $p" ;; esac
  done
  if [ -z "$missing" ]; then ok "$host has gascity, beads, dolt"
  else bad "$host is missing:$missing"; fi
done

other=$(names shiori) || { echo "could not evaluate shiori" >&2; exit 1; }
leaked=""
for p in gascity beads dolt; do
  case " $other " in *" $p "*) leaked="$leaked $p" ;; esac
done
if [ -z "$leaked" ] && [ -n "$other" ]; then ok "shiori carries none of them"
else bad "shiori carries:${leaked:- <nothing evaluated>}"; fi

# Case 3: gc's state (city registry, supervisor config, logs) defaults to ~/.gc;
# GC_HOME moves it under XDG state. It has to be a session variable, not just a
# shell one: `gc start` bakes GC_HOME into the supervisor's systemd unit, so a
# shell that lacks it registers the city under ~/.gc instead.
state=$(nix eval --max-jobs 0 --raw "$repo#homeConfigurations.fujiwara.config.xdg.stateHome") \
  || { echo "could not evaluate fujiwara xdg.stateHome" >&2; exit 1; }
gchome=$(nix eval --max-jobs 0 --raw "$repo#homeConfigurations.fujiwara.config.home.sessionVariables.GC_HOME" 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$gchome" ] && [ "$gchome" = "$state/gc" ]; then ok "fujiwara GC_HOME is \$XDG_STATE_HOME/gc"
else bad "fujiwara GC_HOME: want $state/gc, got ${gchome:-<unset>}"; fi

# Case 4: upstream treats any GC_HOME off ~/.gc as an isolated home and moves
# the supervisor socket and lock under it. patches/gascity-runtime-dir.patch
# adds GC_RUNTIME_DIR to keep them in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; without the variable
# set, case 3 alone puts sockets in ~/.local/state.
rt=$(nix eval --max-jobs 0 --raw "$repo#homeConfigurations.fujiwara.config.home.sessionVariables.GC_RUNTIME_DIR" 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$rt" = '$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gc' ]; then ok "fujiwara GC_RUNTIME_DIR is \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gc"
else bad "fujiwara GC_RUNTIME_DIR: want \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gc, got ${rt:-<unset>}"; fi

# Case 5: gc phones home usage metrics by default, and this box does work.
# patches/gascity-no-usage-metrics.patch compiles collection off; the env opt-out
# is the second layer, for the day the patch stops applying and someone drops it.
nm=$(nix eval --max-jobs 0 --raw "$repo#homeConfigurations.fujiwara.config.home.sessionVariables.GC_DISABLE_USAGE_METRICS" 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$nm" = "1" ]; then ok "fujiwara GC_DISABLE_USAGE_METRICS=1"
else bad "fujiwara GC_DISABLE_USAGE_METRICS: want 1, got ${nm:-<unset>}"; fi

[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

  # stays logged in.
  ++ lib.optionals (!isDarwin && isDesktop && isWorkHost) [
    pkgs.slack
  ]
  # waypipe and the work-slack forward: the pair membership, the

See the full install guide at [docs/getting-started/installation.md](docs/getting-started/installation.md).

### Prerequisites

Gas City requires the following tools on your system. `gc init` and
`gc start` check for these automatically and report any that are missing.

| Dependency | Required | Min Version | Install (macOS) | Install (Linux) |
|------------|----------|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| tmux | Always | — | `brew install tmux` | `apt install tmux` |
| git | Always | — | `brew install git` | `apt install git` |
| jq | Always | — | `brew install jq` | `apt install jq` |
| pgrep | Always | — | (included in macOS) | `apt install procps` |
| lsof | Always | — | (included in macOS) | `apt install lsof` |
| dolt | Beads provider `bd` | 2.1.0 or newer | `brew install dolt` | [releases](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases) |

content.text:
I added `lsof` to the Gas City hosts (fujiwara and utsuho) in `home.nix`, then committed and pushed it as `74bd4c88`. It isn't installed on this box yet.

- **Why gc needs it:** gc's cleanup of leftover dolt databases runs `lsof -w`, and if `lsof` is missing it just stops without removing anything. `gc doctor` also uses it to check ports. The upstream README lists it as always required.
- **The other dependencies:** I checked the rest of the upstream list (tmux, git, jq, pgrep, dolt, bd, flock) and only `lsof` was missing here.
- **Test:** `tests/gascity-packages.sh` now checks that both hosts have `lsof`. All 6 cases pass.
- **Not done:** I didn't run a drovr code review on this 3-line change.
